query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Both files go in `/etc/systemd/system/`, the directory for units the administrator installs. Give them the same base name, because a timer starts the service whose name matches its own.

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.service`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle

# Hardening. ProtectSystem=strict makes the whole filesystem read-only for
# this unit, so the backup can still read everything but can only write to
# the paths listed here. Each path must already exist when the unit starts.
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=/var/backups
StateDirectory=nightly-backup
```

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.timer`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly-backup every night at 02:00

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=5min
AccuracySec=1min

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

The timer reads `OnCalendar` in the machine's local time zone. `Persistent=true` runs a missed backup at the next boot if the machine was off at 2:00. `RandomizedDelaySec` adds a random start delay of up to five minutes. Delete it if the backup must start at exactly 2:00.

Change `ReadWritePaths=` to the backup's real write targets before you enable anything. `/var/backups` is a placeholder. If a listed path doesn't exist, the service fails at startup with "Failed to set up mount namespacing" before the script runs. Also add the path to any lock or state file the script writes outside `/var/lib/nightly-backup`. The service has no `[Install]` section because it's never enabled on its own. The timer starts it.

To install and check the units:

```bash
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.{service,timer}
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer
systemctl list-timers nightly-backup.timer
sudo systemctl start nightly-backup.service     # one test run now
journalctl -u nightly-backup.service
```

If this is for one of your Bluefin machines, write the unit files in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/systemd/system/` first and then copy them into `/etc`, as you do for other `/etc` changes. Bluefin keeps local edits to `/etc` through image updates. `/usr/local/bin` links to `/var/usrlocal/bin` there, so the `ExecStart` path works without changes.
